== Who I am ==

My name is Alessio Faina, and I have been a member of the Ubuntu Kernel Team
since August 2025.

I hold a master degree in Computer Engineering from the University of Pisa.

Before joining Canonical, during almost two decades of my career, I've been fortunate to work on different projects involving the Windows and Linux kernel; I've been exposed to the industry as a developer (Zucchetti, Microsoft), a tech lead and an architect (Displaylink, Synaptics).

=== My Ubuntu story ===

I started using Linux with Slackware around 1999, then during my university time, around 2005, I started using Ubuntu/Kubuntu/Xubuntu as a daily driver. During the years I tried different distros like Gentoo, Linux mint, and Arch Linux, but professionally I've been working mostly with Ubuntu, in particular Focal, Jammy and Noble. 

During my previous role in DisplayLink/Synaptics I practically used Ubuntu as my daily development environment.

=== My involvement ===

Apart for the Bluefield crank/integrations, I've been developing the NVIDIA doca-ofed kernel DKMS repackaging project; other than that I've developed the linux-main-modules project, a package similar in shape to linux-restricted-modules, used to crank DKMS packages outside of the linux-main package.

During my time in Canonical, I've been able to backport multiple CVE fixes and commit them to regular and ESM mailing list, and I've been part of the ACKing/NACKing process to check the submissions of other users.
